name: Low-Poly Shapes
description: A flat-shaded low-poly shape turns over a dimmed plate, one per scene: it pops in, drifts or the camera pushes closer. three.js projects it on the CPU and resvg rasterises each frame.

cautions: The shape is abstract: it illustrates the narration's idea, it never stands for a real object or a real number.
The plate is dimmed behind the shape; keep it a texture, not a picture the viewer must read.

provenance.ref: https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js@r183 (ea4846f2b8feaada5dcce23b61444be361dbbfed; npm three 0.183.2): build/three.module.js and examples/jsm/renderers/Projector.js, used as installed by the environment

provenance.notes: Used as a library, not copied: render/scene.mjs builds a scene with three's polyhedron geometries, a camera and three's Projector (the CPU projection SVGRenderer uses), then writes its own SVG with flat Lambert shading. Nothing of three.js is vendored in the pack.

provenance.licence: MPL-2.0 (LICENSE.txt in the resvg repository at v0.44.0)
provenance.notes: The unmodified release binary, downloaded by the recipe and pinned by sha256; it only rasterises the frames' SVG to PNG.

provenance.ref: venturazz/venstudio docs/plans/style-system.md and this repo's docs/hermes-handover.md (owner decision: learning flows Hermes -> styles repo -> Muse; no tools pre-built by guess)
provenance.notes: The first pack through the handover channel, chosen small and CPU-only to prove the channel: an npm step, a pinned download, a probe and the command renderer. Written by Kiro in Hermes's place for this proof; a real handover carries what Hermes actually used.

licences.notes: npm tarball pinned by the lockfile's sha512 integrity, taken from google/model-viewer package-lock.json at 5cc277a497f6e13fc75ff4821da73164a12570c9 (npm ci refuses a tarball that does not match).
sha256 and size computed from the release asset downloaded through the authenticated GitHub API (asset 195490105); the release predates GitHub's published asset digests. Needs glibc 2.29 or later.
